source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly trains standard neural network architectures on natural and randomized labels, and reports training and test performance.
record.gate_note: The paper reports CIFAR-10 results for natural labels and random-label fitting, including regularizer settings, plus ImageNet natural-label and random-label results. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows. Theoretical expressivity results establish capacity but do not themselves measure the claimed natural-label generalization.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares fitting fixed random labels with natural-label generalization (V1). Its CIFAR-10 results also compare convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch with momentum SGD (V3), although they do not isolate local connectivity.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors find sufficient capacity to memorize random labels alongside natural-label generalization, argue that traditional complexity measures and explicit regularization do not adequately explain this generalization, and distinguish easy optimization from the causes of generalization. They acknowledge incomplete ImageNet fitting and an AlexNet convergence exception with weight decay.
record.recipe_differences: The study directly trains standard architectures with SGD on natural and randomized labels, matching the central method described for V1. Random-label Inception V3 on ImageNet does not reach perfect training accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Natural-label test accuracy varies with architecture and regularization settings. On CIFAR10, batch normalization changes test accuracy by 3–4% according to the text. Alexnet fails to converge on random labels with default weight decay; ImageNet Inception V3 reaches 95.20% top-1 training accuracy on random labels, not 100%.
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated results. ImageNet random-label fitting is incomplete, and the CIFAR10 MLP random-label training accuracies of 99.82%, 99.34% and 99.21% are not exactly 100%. Some regularizer results report training accuracy only. Test accuracy is reported as test accuracy in the paper, with the validation split described in the setup.
record.rows_left_out: None of the study's direct findings relevant to V1 were omitted. The paper's kernel-model test errors and theoretical finite-sample expressivity theorem do not measure a version's named behavior and are therefore not rows.

untested.parts: No width sweep or held-out error comparison beyond the interpolation threshold.
Does not isolate local connectivity, train fully connected networks to learn sparse local connections, or initialize them from trained convolutional networks. Comparisons cover CIFAR-10 only.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No isolated dropout ablation on natural-label held-out performance; joint removal with weight decay does not identify dropout's effect. Small-data and excessive-dropout regimes are untested.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or rankings of generalization gaps.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: Partial-label-corruption sweep: Inception, AlexNet and MLP 1x512 fit corrupted training labels with zero training error, while held-out error increases toward 90% as corruption approaches complete randomization.

record.verdict_notes: No V1 verdict is assigned because this study is V1's original source. Contrary to the record's coverage notes, Tables 1 and 2 explicitly report numerical random-label test accuracies. V3 is tested by the reported architecture comparisons even though architectural causes are not isolated. Near-perfect fitting should not be classified as partial merely because accuracy is below exactly 100%.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report random-label test accuracy as a numerical result in the tables; it states that this is no better than chance. It tests CIFAR-10 Inception, Alexnet, and MLPs, and ImageNet Inception V3; not every architecture or setting named in the version.
The paper gives a finite-sample expressivity theorem but does not sweep network width past the interpolation threshold and measure test error.
No controlled comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures on image test error.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Dropout is present in some ImageNet settings, but the study does not isolate its effect on test error; no dropout comparison on CIFAR-10.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with other generalization measures.
No removal of memorized examples or retraining comparison.
